q: A FinOps analyst at a retailer needs to review the last 13 months of ML spend per tag and see a forecast for the next 18 months. Which AWS tool fits best?
options: AWS Cost Explorer
AWS Budgets
AWS Trusted Advisor checks
AWS Config rules
explain: Cost Explorer shows up to 13 months of history, filters by tag, and forecasts spend for the next 18 months. Budgets alerts on thresholds, Trusted Advisor recommends, and Config tracks configuration.
source: AWS docs: Cost Management User Guide - Analyzing your costs with Cost Explorer

q: A data science team must be emailed when its monthly ML spend reaches 80 percent of a fixed target. Which AWS service should the team configure?
options: AWS Cost Explorer forecast view, which projects future spend but never sends threshold alerts
AWS Budgets cost budget with notifications
Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights query run over the billing log group every hour
AWS Compute Optimizer recommendation applied to the training instances
explain: A cost budget with a threshold notification sends alerts by email or Amazon SNS. Cost Explorer analyzes spend after the fact and does not alert on a threshold.
source: AWS docs: Cost Management User Guide - Managing your costs with AWS Budgets

q: A company wants a service that inspects its AWS account and recommends improvements in cost, security, and fault tolerance. Which service is this?
options: AWS Config conformance rules for resource evaluation
AWS Service Catalog portfolios of approved products
AWS Trusted Advisor
AWS Systems Manager Explorer dashboards
explain: Trusted Advisor inspects the environment and recommends best-practice improvements. Config records resource configuration history and evaluates rules, which is a different function.
source: AWS docs: AWS Support User Guide - AWS Trusted Advisor

q: A team runs a SageMaker real-time endpoint whose instances show low CPU and memory use for weeks. It wants AWS to suggest a smaller instance type from 14 days of metrics, without running a load test. Which service should it use?
options: SageMaker Inference Recommender Advanced job
Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights queries
AWS Budgets forecast reports
AWS Compute Optimizer recommendations
explain: Compute Optimizer analyzes utilization metrics from existing resources and suggests rightsizing. An Inference Recommender job runs load tests rather than analyzing existing usage.
source: AWS docs: Compute Optimizer User Guide - What is AWS Compute Optimizer?

q: A team must pick the endpoint instance type for a new model. It needs a load test that uses its own traffic pattern and checks latency and throughput targets before launch. Which Inference Recommender job should it run?
options: Advanced recommendation job with a custom load test
Default recommendation job, which needs only a model package
Compute Optimizer opt-in for the account
Managed Spot Training job with checkpoints
explain: The Advanced job runs a custom load test with a traffic pattern and latency or throughput requirements. The Default job is a quick preliminary benchmark that needs only the model package.
source: AWS docs: SageMaker AI Developer Guide - Recommendation jobs with Inference Recommender

q: A company runs training jobs for three teams. Tags were applied last week, but monthly cost reports in Cost Explorer do not show them. What should the ML engineer check first?
options: Whether the instance type supports network isolation
Whether the tag key has been activated as a cost allocation tag in the Billing console
Whether the S3 bucket has versioning enabled
Whether the endpoint has provisioned concurrency
explain: A user-defined cost allocation tag appears in cost reports only after it is activated in Billing. The other options concern security, storage, or Lambda features that do not affect cost reporting.
source: AWS docs: Billing User Guide - Backfill cost allocation tags

q: Which TWO statements about cost allocation tags are correct? (Select TWO.)
options: After a tag is applied to resources, the tag key can take up to 24 hours to appear on the cost allocation tags page
Backfill can cover up to 12 months of history, but only for resources that already carried the tag in that period
Activating a user-defined tag in Billing applies it retroactively to every previous month automatically
AWS-generated tags are created and applied by the customer through resource configuration templates
Cost allocation tags appear in Cost Explorer as soon as a resource is created, with no activation step
explain: Tag keys can take up to 24 hours to appear, and backfill covers at most 12 months but only where the tag existed. Activation is not retroactive by default, and AWS-generated tags are applied by AWS.
source: AWS docs: Billing User Guide - Backfill cost allocation tags

q: Finance asks the ML platform team where to find the monthly invoices and payment details for the account, and where to activate cost allocation tags. Which AWS console covers both?
options: AWS Trusted Advisor checks console
Amazon CloudWatch metrics console
AWS Billing and Cost Management
AWS Config resource inventory console
explain: Billing and Cost Management covers invoices, payments, and tag activation. The other consoles serve different purposes.
source: AWS docs: Cost Management User Guide - Analyzing your costs with Cost Explorer

q: A team runs SageMaker Studio notebooks and real-time inference steadily for at least a year. It wants a discount without tying itself to specific instance types. Which option fits best?
options: Managed Spot Training
Reserved Instances for one EC2 instance type
On-Demand pricing with no commitment
SageMaker Savings Plans
explain: SageMaker Savings Plans commit to a dollar amount per hour for one or three years and apply across eligible SageMaker usage. Reserved Instances are tied to EC2 instance configurations.
source: AWS docs: Savings Plans - Amazon SageMaker Savings Plans

q: A training job can tolerate interruptions and writes checkpoints to Amazon S3. Which purchasing option is designed for this pattern?
options: Managed Spot Training
On-Demand training with no checkpoints
Compute Savings Plans for the management account
Reserved Instances for the C family
explain: Managed Spot Training uses Spot capacity at a discount and resumes from S3 checkpoints after an interruption. The other options do not combine interruption tolerance with a discount.
source: AWS docs: SageMaker AI Developer Guide - Managed Spot Training

q: Which THREE statements about SageMaker purchasing options are correct? (Select THREE.)
options: Reserved Instances apply to any SageMaker instance family automatically
Savings Plans reduce the hourly rate only for Spot instances, and never for On-Demand usage at all
SageMaker Savings Plans commit to a dollar amount per hour for one or three years
Usage above a Savings Plans commitment is billed at On-Demand rates
SageMaker Savings Plans cover Studio notebooks, Processing, Training, real-time inference, and Batch Transform
A Savings Plans commitment must be raised before each training job starts, or the job is stopped
explain: Savings Plans are hourly dollar commitments covering several SageMaker services, with excess usage at On-Demand rates. Reserved Instances do not automatically cover every SageMaker family, and Savings Plans do not apply only to Spot.
source: AWS docs: Savings Plans - Amazon SageMaker Savings Plans

q: A team wants to compare its cost this quarter with the same quarter last year and find the top services driving the change. Which tool fits best?
options: AWS Config
Cost Explorer
AWS CloudTrail
Amazon Inspector
explain: Cost Explorer compares periods and groups costs by service, which identifies cost drivers. Config, CloudTrail, and Inspector do not analyze spend.
source: AWS docs: Cost Management User Guide - Analyzing your costs with Cost Explorer

q: Which TWO statements about AWS cost tools are correct? (Select TWO.)
options: AWS Budgets can send notifications by email or Amazon SNS when a threshold is crossed
Cost Explorer forecasts spend for the next 18 months
Basic Support customers receive every Trusted Advisor check automatically
Budgets data refreshes in real time, every minute, so spend alerts arrive immediately after each charge
Trusted Advisor replaces Cost Explorer as the source of spend forecasts
explain: Budgets notifies on thresholds through email or SNS, and Cost Explorer forecasts 18 months. Full Trusted Advisor checks require higher support plans, Budgets data is updated a few times per day, and Trusted Advisor does not forecast spend.
source: AWS docs: AWS Support User Guide - AWS Trusted Advisor

q: A Lambda function for an interactive API has cold-start latency at peak traffic. Which configuration reduces this, and where should it be applied?
options: Reserved concurrency set to zero for the whole account
Provisioned concurrency applied to the unpublished $LATEST version of the function
Provisioned concurrency on a published version or alias of the function
Increasing only the memory of the unpublished $LATEST version of the function
explain: Provisioned concurrency keeps pre-initialized environments ready for requests, but it must target a published version or alias, not $LATEST.
source: AWS docs: Lambda Developer Guide - Configuring provisioned concurrency

q: An ML team's training launch fails because the account has reached a service quota for an instance type. Which TWO actions address this? (Select TWO.)
options: Create a Budgets alert on monthly spend
Turn on Trusted Advisor full checks for the account
Request a quota increase in Service Quotas if the quota is adjustable
Request a quota increase through the Service Quotas API
Add a Savings Plans commitment for the instance family
explain: Adjustable quotas can be increased from Service Quotas in the console or through the API. Alerts, Trusted Advisor checks, and commitments do not raise a quota.
source: AWS docs: Service Quotas User Guide - What is Service Quotas?

q: A team must decide whether a SageMaker endpoint spends more time in its model code or in SageMaker overhead. Which metric answers this directly for the model container?
options: OverheadLatency
Invocation5XXErrors
InvocationsPerInstance
ModelLatency
explain: ModelLatency is the time the model container takes to respond. OverheadLatency is the time added by SageMaker. Error and invocation metrics do not measure time spent in the model.
source: AWS docs: SageMaker AI Developer Guide - SageMaker AI metrics in Amazon CloudWatch

q: An ML engineer wants to compare request load across the instances of one production variant. Which metric reports invocations normalized by the number of instances?
options: InvocationsPerInstance
Invocations summed across the whole endpoint
CPUUtilization of the production variant
ModelLatency of each invocation
explain: InvocationsPerInstance normalizes invocations by the active instance count, which makes load comparable. The plain Invocations metric is a total for the endpoint.
source: AWS docs: SageMaker AI Developer Guide - SageMaker AI metrics in Amazon CloudWatch

q: Which TWO signals indicate that a SageMaker endpoint may be under-provisioned for its traffic? (Select TWO.)
options: CPUUtilization approaching its ceiling during peak traffic
Invocation4XXErrors rising when clients send valid requests
CloudTrail trail status changing to disabled
A Budgets threshold being crossed in the month
ModelLatency rising under sustained load
explain: High CPU and rising model latency under load show capacity pressure. Client-side 4XX errors and budget or trail events do not indicate capacity.
source: AWS docs: SageMaker AI Developer Guide - SageMaker AI metrics in Amazon CloudWatch

q: Which THREE actions improve the availability of a SageMaker real-time endpoint? (Select THREE.)
options: Increase MaxRuntimeInSeconds on the endpoint configuration
Set the production variant initial instance count to at least 2 so SageMaker can spread instances across Availability Zones
Enable Managed Spot Training on the endpoint
Increase CloudWatch log retention for the endpoint
Turn on Inter-container traffic encryption for the endpoint
Configure auto scaling with a minimum instance count above 1
explain: More than one instance lets SageMaker provide multi-AZ redundancy, and a minimum above 1 keeps that capacity under auto scaling. Runtime limits, Spot training, logging, and traffic encryption do not improve availability.
source: AWS docs: Security Hub User Guide - SageMaker AI controls

q: A team runs large in-memory analytics on its ML features and must choose an EC2 family before rebuilding its cluster. Which family is designed for large in-memory workloads?
options: C family, compute optimized for CPU-bound work
R family, memory optimized for large in-memory data sets
M family, general purpose with balanced resources
G family, accelerated for graphics work
explain: The R family is memory optimized, C is compute optimized, M is general purpose, and G is accelerated for graphics and floating-point work.
source: AWS docs: Amazon EC2 instance types

q: An agent built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore must be monitored in production for session count, latency, token usage, and error rates. Which capability provides these built-in metrics and dashboards?
options: Amazon Inspector Code Security
AWS Trusted Advisor
AgentCore Observability
AWS CloudTrail trail
explain: AgentCore Observability provides built-in metrics for agents and dashboards in CloudWatch, using OpenTelemetry-compatible telemetry. The other services serve different purposes.
source: AWS docs: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Developer Guide - Observability

q: Which TWO are valid ways to troubleshoot an ML workload with observability tools? (Select TWO.)
options: Disable CloudWatch metrics to reduce noise during an incident
Replace all traces with a monthly Budgets report
Use AWS Config to see the latency of each inference request
Use AWS X-Ray to trace a request across services and find the slow one
Use CloudWatch Logs Insights to query application logs for a failing request
explain: X-Ray traces requests across services and Logs Insights queries logs. Disabling metrics, using budget reports, and using Config for latency do not troubleshoot runtime behavior.
source: AWS docs: AWS X-Ray Developer Guide - What is AWS X-Ray?

q: Which THREE capabilities does AWS X-Ray provide? (Select THREE.)
options: A trace map of the services a request calls downstream
Segments and subsegments that record the work done for each request
Ten-year retention of application logs
Automatic creation of CloudWatch alarms
Enforcement of IAM permissions on Lambda functions
Identification of latency bottlenecks from trace data
explain: X-Ray builds trace maps, records segments and subsegments, and helps locate bottlenecks. It does not retain logs for years, create alarms, or enforce IAM permissions.
source: AWS docs: AWS X-Ray Developer Guide - What is AWS X-Ray?

q: A microservice chain behind an ML inference API shows intermittent latency spikes. Which tool draws each downstream call and highlights the slow service?
options: CloudWatch Logs Insights field index
AWS Budgets action
AWS CloudTrail data event
AWS X-Ray trace map of the downstream services
explain: The X-Ray trace map shows the client, the front-end service, and the backends it calls, so the slow hop is visible. The other options do not show request paths.
source: AWS docs: AWS X-Ray Developer Guide - What is AWS X-Ray?

q: A team wants per-invocation CPU, memory, and cold-start diagnostics for a Lambda function without writing custom metrics code. Which service should it enable?
options: CloudWatch Lambda Insights extension
AWS Config conformance pack
AWS Organizations service control policy
Amazon Inspector vulnerability scan
explain: Lambda Insights uses a CloudWatch extension in a layer to collect system metrics and diagnostics such as cold starts for each invocation.
source: AWS docs: CloudWatch Developer Guide - Lambda Insights

q: Which TWO statements about CloudWatch Logs Insights are correct? (Select TWO.)
options: The service supports only SQL as a query language
Queries are free regardless of how much log data they scan
Queries time out after 60 minutes if they have not completed
Query results are available for 7 days
Queries cannot reach log groups in other accounts under any setup
explain: Logs Insights queries time out after 60 minutes and results are kept for 7 days. It supports three query languages and charges by data scanned, and cross-account querying is possible with a monitoring account.
source: AWS docs: CloudWatch Logs User Guide - Analyzing log data with CloudWatch Logs Insights

q: Business stakeholders need interactive dashboards built on a data lake and want to filter the data themselves. Which service fits best?
options: Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights
Amazon Quick Sight, the business intelligence component of Amazon Quick
AWS Budgets
Amazon Simple Notification Service
explain: Amazon Quick Sight is the business intelligence component of Amazon Quick, the former QuickSight. The other services do not provide interactive business dashboards.
source: AWS docs: Amazon Quick - What is Amazon Quick?

q: An on-call operator wants one page that shows several operational metrics as graphs. Which CloudWatch feature provides this?
options: AWS CloudTrail event history
AWS Config timeline
CloudWatch dashboard
AWS Budgets report
explain: A CloudWatch dashboard arranges metric graphs and query widgets on one page for monitoring. The other options record events or costs.
source: AWS docs: SageMaker AI Developer Guide - SageMaker AI metrics in Amazon CloudWatch

q: CloudWatch alarm notifications for an ML team must be posted to a Slack channel, with a button that runs a Lambda function. Which service handles this?
options: AWS Config rules and conformance packs
AWS Secrets Manager rotation schedules
AWS CloudTrail trails and event selectors
Amazon Q Developer in chat applications
explain: Amazon Q Developer in chat applications, formerly AWS Chatbot, receives SNS notifications, posts them to chat channels, and supports custom actions. The other services do not deliver chat notifications.
source: AWS docs: Amazon Q Developer in chat applications - What is?

q: Which TWO chat platforms does Amazon Q Developer in chat applications support? (Select TWO.)
options: Slack
Telegram
WhatsApp
Discord
Microsoft Teams
explain: The service supports Slack, Microsoft Teams, and Amazon Chime. The other platforms are not supported.
source: AWS docs: Amazon Q Developer in chat applications - What is?

q: The FinOps lead wants a smaller SageMaker instance type for an under-used endpoint, based on existing utilization and with no load test. Which service can make rightsizing recommendations from 14 days of metrics?
options: AWS Compute Optimizer, which suggests rightsizing from utilization metrics
AWS CloudTrail event history
Amazon Inspector Code Security
AWS Config conformance packs
explain: Compute Optimizer supports SageMaker among its resource types and analyzes utilization metrics, using 14 days by default.
source: AWS docs: Compute Optimizer User Guide - What is AWS Compute Optimizer?

q: Which THREE statements about AWS Compute Optimizer are correct? (Select THREE.)
options: It creates new endpoints automatically when it finds an under-used one
It requires the account or organization to opt in before it analyzes resources
Its default analysis uses 14 days of utilization metrics
It replaces Inference Recommender load tests for new models
It analyzes data only from the management account of an organization
It supports Amazon SageMaker resources among its resource types
explain: Compute Optimizer requires opt-in, uses 14 days by default, and supports SageMaker. It does not create endpoints, replace load tests, or limit analysis to the management account.
source: AWS docs: Compute Optimizer User Guide - What is AWS Compute Optimizer?

q: A team wants a managed service that uses machine learning to find operational anomalies in application metrics and events and then recommends fixes. Which service fits?
options: Trusted Advisor
Amazon DevOps Guru
AWS Budgets
Compute Optimizer
explain: DevOps Guru applies machine learning to operational data, detects deviations, and produces insights with recommendations. The other services do not detect operational anomalies.
source: AWS docs: Amazon DevOps Guru User Guide - What is Amazon DevOps Guru?

q: An operations team wants advance warning of issues that might hit its application later, not only the ones happening now. Which DevOps Guru output predicts future operational issues?
options: Reactive insights
Budget alerts
Proactive insights
Trusted Advisor
explain: DevOps Guru creates reactive insights for current issues and proactive insights for likely future issues. Budget alerts and Trusted Advisor checks are different services.
source: AWS docs: Amazon DevOps Guru User Guide - What is Amazon DevOps Guru?

q: A team will run one EC2 instance configuration all year and wants a discount on it. Which purchase option is designed for EC2 reservations of specific instance configurations?
options: SageMaker Savings Plans
Managed Spot Training
On-Demand Instances
Reserved Instances, which apply to EC2 configurations
explain: Reserved Instances apply to EC2 configurations. Savings Plans commit a dollar amount per hour, and Spot and On-Demand do not involve reservations.
source: AWS docs: Savings Plans - Amazon SageMaker Savings Plans

q: A team must serve an already trained model at the lowest cost per prediction. Which compute option should it evaluate first?
options: Inferentia-based Inf2 instances, designed for high-throughput inference
C family compute optimized instances without accelerators
P5 GPU instances for large model training
R family memory optimized instances
explain: Inferentia is an AWS chip designed for inference, and Inf2 offers higher throughput and lower latency than Inf1. The other families are not designed for this inference pattern.
source: AWS docs: AWS Inferentia

q: A company runs a containerized CPU-bound inference API. It wants the lowest cost for the same performance and is willing to rebuild its images for ARM64. Which option fits best?
options: x86 instances of the same size, with the same performance profile
Graviton-based instances
P5 GPU instances with eight accelerators for training
Trainium-based training clusters for large distributed jobs
explain: Graviton is AWS's ARM processor family, with a documented price-performance advantage over comparable x86 instances. The GPU and training options do not match a CPU-bound inference workload.
source: AWS docs: AWS Graviton

q: A data science team trains a deep learning model that needs GPU memory for large language models. Which EC2 family is designed for high-performance GPU training?
options: M general purpose with balanced compute, memory, and networking
C compute optimized for CPU-bound batch processing work
P accelerated GPU for high-performance deep learning training
R memory optimized for large in-memory data set analysis
explain: The P family provides high-performance GPUs for deep learning and HPC, and P5 is described for training large models. The other families do not carry GPUs for this purpose.
source: AWS docs: Amazon EC2 instance types

q: A study group reviews the Well-Architected material for the MLA-C01 exam. Which document provides design principles for ML workloads and is listed under monitoring in the MLA-C01 guide?
options: AWS Shared Responsibility Model guide
AWS Trusted Advisor cost and security report
SageMaker Model Card documentation template
Well-Architected Machine Learning Lens
explain: The Well-Architected Machine Learning Lens defines design principles for ML workloads, and the MLA-C01 guide ties design principles for ML lenses to monitoring. The other documents cover different topics.
source: AWS docs: Well-Architected Machine Learning Lens - Design principles

q: An ML platform team wants to version infrastructure, data, models, and code so that it can return to any point-in-time release. Which Well-Architected ML Lens principle addresses this?
options: Enable reproducibility
Enable reusability
Optimize resources
Minimize environmental impact
explain: Enable reproducibility asks for version control across components so releases can be traced back. Reusability concerns modular components, and the other two principles address different goals.
source: AWS docs: Well-Architected Machine Learning Lens - Design principles

q: A monitoring job reports a constraint violation on a production endpoint. Which action gives the fastest notification to the team?
options: Deleting the monitoring schedule
A CloudWatch alarm on the violation metric that notifies an SNS topic
Increasing the endpoint instance count
Disabling Data Capture on the endpoint
explain: A CloudWatch alarm on the violation metric sends a notification when the violation appears. The other options do not notify anyone and some remove the monitoring signal.
source: AWS docs: SageMaker AI Developer Guide - SageMaker AI metrics in Amazon CloudWatch

q: A training job fails because of a bug in the training script, not because of a service error. Which retry behavior applies?
options: The job is retried up to MaximumRetryAttempts for any failure, including errors in the training script code
The job restarts automatically on a different instance family chosen by the service at launch time
The job is retried only for InternalServerError, so the bug must be fixed and the job submitted again
The job retries after the Spot interruption window expires, using the same checkpoint and configuration
explain: RetryStrategy retries a training job only when it fails with an InternalServerError. A code bug is not retried automatically, so the code or input must be corrected.
source: AWS docs: SageMaker AI API Reference - CreateTrainingJob

q: A SageMaker pipeline has a failing step. Which pipeline metric is the right one to put on an alarm?
options: CPUUtilization of the endpoint instances in the production variant group
ModelLatency of the endpoint for each invocation request received
Invocation4XXErrors of the endpoint for client request validation
StepFailed in the AWS/Sagemaker/ModelBuildingPipeline namespace
explain: StepFailed counts failed steps in the pipeline namespace, which makes it the pipeline-level signal. The endpoint metrics describe inference, not pipeline steps.
source: AWS docs: SageMaker AI Developer Guide - SageMaker AI metrics in Amazon CloudWatch

q: A company wants a record of every API call in its ML account, delivered to an S3 bucket. Which AWS feature creates this delivery?
options: A CloudTrail trail that delivers management event logs to an S3 bucket
A CloudWatch dashboard
An AWS Config conformance pack
A Trusted Advisor report
explain: A CloudTrail trail delivers management event logs to an S3 bucket. The other features do not record API calls to S3.
source: AWS docs: CloudTrail User Guide - Creating a trail

q: An auditor needs to see reads of individual objects in a training data bucket, which are not recorded by default. Which setting is required?
options: Management events only, which the trail already records by default
Data events for the S3 resource type in the trail
A Savings Plans commitment applied to the S3 storage class
A Logs Insights field index on the bucket name
explain: Object-level S3 reads are data events, which are not logged by default and must be selected for the trail. Management events do not include object reads.
source: AWS docs: CloudTrail User Guide - Logging data events

q: A security team must answer two audit questions: who called an API, and what a security group looked like last month. Which THREE actions meet these needs? (Select THREE.)
options: Enable data events on the training data bucket to see who changed the security group
Use CloudWatch dashboards to view past IAM policy versions and the security group rules they contain for auditors
Use Trusted Advisor full checks to read the historical state of the security group
Create a multi-Region CloudTrail trail that delivers logs to an S3 bucket
Use AWS Config configuration history to see the security group configuration on a past date
Send CloudTrail events to CloudWatch Logs and create alarms on specific API calls
explain: CloudTrail answers who called the API and Config answers the past configuration. Sending CloudTrail to CloudWatch Logs adds alarms. Data events on the bucket do not record security group changes, and dashboards and Trusted Advisor do not keep this history.
source: AWS docs: AWS Config Developer Guide - What is AWS Config?

q: An auditor asks for the history of resource configurations and their compliance against internal rules. Which AWS service records configuration history and evaluates resources against rules?
options: AWS CloudTrail
Amazon CloudWatch Logs
AWS Config
AWS X-Ray
explain: AWS Config records resource configurations and their history, and evaluates them with rules. CloudTrail records API calls, which is a different question.
source: AWS docs: AWS Config Developer Guide - What is AWS Config?

q: An auditor needs proof of who changed an IAM role and what its policy looked like before the change. Which combination fits best?
options: CloudWatch dashboards for the API call history plus Trusted Advisor for the configuration history
AWS Budgets for the API call history plus Cost Explorer for the configuration history
AWS X-Ray traces for the API call history plus Logs Insights for the configuration history
CloudTrail for the API call history plus AWS Config for the configuration history
explain: CloudTrail shows the API call that made the change, and Config shows the configuration before and after. Together they answer both audit questions.
source: AWS docs: AWS Config Developer Guide - What is AWS Config?

q: A training job processes regulated data and must not make any outbound network call, including calls to Amazon S3 from inside the container. Which setting meets this requirement?
options: EnableNetworkIsolation set to True
Inter-container traffic encryption
A Savings Plans commitment
Managed Spot Training with checkpoints
explain: Network isolation blocks inbound and outbound calls from the container, including to S3, and makes no AWS credentials available inside it. The other options address cost or encryption between nodes.
source: AWS docs: SageMaker AI API Reference - CreateTrainingJob

q: A distributed training job must be isolated from the internet, and its nodes must encrypt traffic between them. Which TWO settings are required? (Select TWO.)
options: EnableNetworkIsolation set to True
EnableInterContainerTrafficEncryption set to True
Public subnets with an internet gateway attached
Managed Spot Training enabled for the job
A NAT gateway for outbound access from the training containers
explain: Network isolation blocks the container from internet and AWS service calls, while inter-container encryption protects communication between nodes. Public subnets and NAT gateways add outbound access, which the requirement rules out.
source: AWS docs: SageMaker AI Developer Guide - Protect communications between ML compute instances

q: A single-instance training job is configured with inter-container traffic encryption. What effect does the setting have on training time?
options: It doubles the training time for every job, because all traffic is re-encrypted on each step
None, because there is no communication between instances in a single-instance job
It requires a NAT gateway to be created before the job can start in the VPC subnet
It disables CloudWatch metrics for the job, which then cannot report instance utilization
explain: Inter-container encryption encrypts traffic between compute instances, so a single-instance job has no such traffic and is not affected. The other options describe effects the setting does not have.
source: AWS docs: SageMaker AI Developer Guide - Protect communications between ML compute instances

q: A training job in private subnets must read training data from S3, but the subnets have no internet route. What is the most direct fix?
options: Attach a public IP address to each training instance so it can reach S3 directly
Disable VPC mode for the job so that it runs on the service-managed network
Add an S3 gateway VPC endpoint associated with the subnet route tables
Add an inbound rule on port 443 to the security group used by the training job
explain: An S3 gateway endpoint adds routes that keep S3 traffic inside the VPC, which lets the private job reach its data. Public IPs and VPC removal change the security posture, and inbound rules do not give outbound S3 access.
source: AWS docs: SageMaker AI Developer Guide - Give training jobs access to resources in your VPC

q: In distributed training inside a VPC, training nodes must communicate with each other. Which security group rule enables this?
options: An inbound rule from 0.0.0.0/0 on all ports for every training instance in the job
A rule that allows only the S3 prefix list, so training nodes can reach the bucket
No rule at all, because training nodes communicate through IAM role credentials
A self-referencing rule that allows traffic from the same security group
explain: A self-referencing rule lets members of the same security group reach each other, which distributed training requires. Open-to-the-world rules are not needed and IAM does not carry node traffic.
source: AWS docs: SageMaker AI Developer Guide - Give training jobs access to resources in your VPC

q: A team needs private connectivity from a VPC to the SageMaker API without using the internet. Which endpoint type is used for most AWS services, based on AWS PrivateLink?
options: Interface endpoint, based on AWS PrivateLink for most services
Gateway endpoint, used for S3 and DynamoDB in the VPC route tables
NAT gateway, which sends outbound traffic to the internet
Internet gateway, which attaches the VPC to the public internet
explain: Interface endpoints use AWS PrivateLink for most services, including the SageMaker API. Gateway endpoints are used for S3 and DynamoDB, and NAT or internet gateways send traffic out to the internet.
source: AWS docs: SageMaker AI Developer Guide - Give training jobs access to resources in your VPC

q: Which TWO are needed for a private-subnet training job to reach S3 without internet access? (Select TWO.)
options: A public IP address on each training instance
An internet gateway attached to the subnet
An S3 gateway endpoint associated with the subnet route tables
A bucket policy or endpoint policy that restricts access to the VPC
A Savings Plans commitment for the training instances
explain: The gateway endpoint provides the route to S3, and a bucket or endpoint policy can restrict access to the VPC. Public IPs and internet gateways give internet access the requirement excludes.
source: AWS docs: SageMaker AI Developer Guide - Give training jobs access to resources in your VPC

q: An IAM principal in a member account has the required action in its identity policy but still gets AccessDenied. Which layer could be blocking it?
options: The bucket name is longer than the allowed length for an S3 request path
A service control policy in the organization that does not allow the action
The instance type selected for the job is larger than the default instance size
The training image in the container registry uses a newer tag than expected
explain: Identity policies grant permissions, but an SCP can deny an action for member accounts even when the identity policy allows it. The other options do not produce AccessDenied.
source: AWS docs: IAM User Guide - Policy evaluation logic

q: Which TWO causes can produce AccessDenied when an ML engineer creates a training job? (Select TWO.)
options: The caller lacks iam:PassRole on the execution role
The notebook kernel version is outdated
The Logs Insights query uses too many fields
The instance family has more GPUs than the job needs
The KMS key policy does not allow the execution role to use the key
explain: Passing the execution role requires iam:PassRole, and a customer managed KMS key requires its key policy to allow the role. Kernel versions, query fields, and GPU counts do not cause AccessDenied.
source: AWS docs: IAM User Guide - Policy evaluation logic

q: Which THREE are evaluated when investigating an AccessDenied error on an AWS API call? (Select THREE.)
options: The notebook kernel name
The identity policy of the calling principal
The resource policy on the target resource
The CPU count of the instance
The Logs Insights query language
The service control policies of the organization
explain: Identity policies, resource policies, and SCPs all take part in the authorization decision. Kernel names, CPU counts, and query languages do not.
source: AWS docs: IAM User Guide - Policy evaluation logic

q: A role's identity policy allows s3:GetObject, but a permissions boundary attached to the role does not include it. What happens when the role calls GetObject?
options: The call is allowed, because the identity policy takes precedence over any permissions boundary attached
The call is allowed only when the request originates from the management account of the organization
The call is denied, because effective permissions are the intersection of the identity policy and the boundary
The call is retried by the service until the permissions boundary is updated by an administrator
explain: A permissions boundary limits the maximum permissions, so the action must be allowed by both the identity policy and the boundary. The call is denied.
source: AWS docs: IAM User Guide - Policy evaluation logic

q: A security lead wants guardrails across all member accounts of an organization. Which statement about service control policies is correct?
options: They grant permissions to every IAM user and role that exists in the management account of the organization
They apply to the root user of the management account and override every other policy type
They replace identity-based policies for member accounts, so those policies are no longer evaluated
They limit the maximum permissions for member accounts and do not grant permissions by themselves
explain: SCPs set the maximum permissions for member accounts and never grant permissions. They do not apply to the management account, and identity policies are still needed.
source: AWS docs: AWS Organizations User Guide - Service control policies

q: An SCP denies s3:DeleteObject for member accounts. An administrator attaches AdministratorAccess to a role in a member account. Can the role delete objects?
options: No, the SCP denial still applies to the role
Yes, AdministratorAccess overrides SCPs
Yes, but only in the management account
Only after the SCP is detached from the account
explain: An SCP is a guardrail that applies to all principals in the member account, and an identity policy cannot override it. The role is denied.
source: AWS docs: AWS Organizations User Guide - Service control policies

q: A company wants persona-based SageMaker execution roles with preconfigured permissions for data scientists and MLOps engineers. Which SageMaker feature was designed for this?
options: SageMaker Pipelines for orchestrating model build steps
SageMaker Role Manager
SageMaker Clarify for bias and explainability reports
SageMaker Feature Store for reusing features across teams
explain: Role Manager creates persona-based IAM roles with suggested permissions. It is no longer open to new customers as of 30 July 2026, and existing customers continue to use it.
source: AWS docs: SageMaker AI Developer Guide - Role Manager availability change

q: A team wants least-privilege policies generated from the actual CloudTrail activity of its SageMaker execution role. Which IAM capability fits best?
options: AWS Budgets forecast for IAM role usage
AWS Config rules that evaluate role configuration
IAM Access Analyzer policy generation
Amazon Inspector scan of IAM role permissions
explain: IAM Access Analyzer generates least-privilege policies from CloudTrail access activity, and AWS names it as the alternative to Role Manager.
source: AWS docs: SageMaker AI Developer Guide - Role Manager availability change

q: A developer must store an API key in Parameter Store so that the value is encrypted with AWS KMS. Which Parameter Store type provides this encryption?
options: StringList
String
Standard tier parameter
SecureString
explain: SecureString parameters are encrypted with AWS KMS. StringList and String store plain text, and the tier is a capacity setting, not an encryption type.
source: AWS docs: Systems Manager User Guide - Parameter Store

q: A team stores a database password and needs automatic rotation every 30 days. Which service fits?
options: AWS Secrets Manager, with automatic rotation for credentials
Systems Manager Parameter Store SecureString
AWS Config
Amazon Inspector
explain: Secrets Manager is designed for credentials and supports automatic rotation. Parameter Store SecureString encrypts values but does not rotate them automatically.
source: AWS docs: AWS Secrets Manager User Guide - What is Secrets Manager?

q: Which TWO statements about Systems Manager Parameter Store are correct? (Select TWO.)
options: SecureString values are rotated automatically
Values are limited to 512 characters on all tiers
Parameter Store keeps only the last 10 versions of a parameter
The standard tier supports up to 10000 parameters per account and Region
The advanced tier supports parameter policies
explain: The standard tier allows 10000 parameters and the advanced tier supports policies. SecureString is not rotated automatically, and Parameter Store keeps up to 100 versions, not 10.
source: AWS docs: Systems Manager User Guide - Parameter Store

q: A team wants container images in Amazon ECR scanned for software vulnerabilities at each push, and rescanned when new CVEs appear. Which service provides this?
options: AWS Config
Amazon Inspector
Secrets Manager
Quick Sight
explain: Amazon Inspector scans ECR images for software vulnerabilities, on push or continuously with enhanced scanning. The other services do not scan images for vulnerabilities.
source: AWS docs: Amazon Inspector User Guide - Scanning ECR images

q: Which TWO statements about Amazon Inspector scanning are correct? (Select TWO.)
options: Enhanced scanning of ECR images covers operating system and programming language packages
Inspector does not scan Lambda functions encrypted with customer managed keys
Basic ECR scanning is billed through Amazon Inspector
Archived ECR images are scanned continuously
Lambda code scanning can be enabled without standard scanning
explain: Enhanced scanning covers OS and language packages and is billed by Inspector. Inspector does not scan Lambda functions encrypted with customer managed keys. Basic scanning is billed by ECR, archived images are not scanned, and code scanning requires standard scanning first.
source: AWS docs: Amazon Inspector User Guide - Scanning Lambda functions

q: A pipeline deploys container images to a SageMaker endpoint. Which design best ensures that a vulnerable image never reaches production? (Select TWO.)
options: Give the pipeline role AdministratorAccess so that deployments never fail
Scan the image only after it has been deployed to production
Scan each image in ECR on push and gate the deployment on the scan result
Give the pipeline role only the actions needed to build, scan, and deploy
Disable image scanning to speed up builds
explain: Gating deployment on a scan blocks vulnerable images before release, and a least-privilege pipeline role limits the damage from a compromised pipeline. Scanning after deployment or disabling scans does not prevent exposure, and administrator access is excessive.
source: AWS docs: MLA-C02 exam guide - skill 4.3.1

q: The MLA-C02 exam guide skill for securing CI/CD pipelines names two services for checking code and image vulnerabilities. Which pair is named?
options: Amazon Macie and AWS Config for pipeline security
AWS Trusted Advisor and AWS Budgets for pipeline cost
Amazon CodeGuru and Amazon Inspector
Amazon Cognito and AWS Shield for pipeline access
explain: Skill 4.3.1 of the MLA-C02 guide names Amazon CodeGuru and Amazon Inspector for securing CI/CD pipelines. The other pairs are not named in that skill.
source: AWS docs: MLA-C02 exam guide - skill 4.3.1

q: A DevSecOps lead reads the MLA-C02 CI/CD security skill and wants the code-review service it names, as opposed to the image scanner. Which service is it?
options: Amazon Inspector for image and code scanning
AWS Config for resource compliance evaluation
AWS CloudTrail for API call auditing
Amazon CodeGuru
explain: CodeGuru is named in skill 4.3.1 for code review, while Inspector is named for vulnerability scanning of images and code. Config and CloudTrail are not CI/CD code tools.
source: AWS docs: MLA-C02 exam guide - skill 4.3.1

q: A team uses Savings Plans and must be alerted when the share of its eligible usage covered by Savings Plans drops below a target. Which budget type fits?
options: Savings Plans coverage budget
Cost budget for the whole account
Usage budget for Lambda invocations
RI utilization budget
explain: A Savings Plans coverage budget alerts when coverage falls below a threshold. A cost budget tracks spend, a usage budget tracks consumption, and an RI utilization budget applies to Reserved Instances.
source: AWS docs: Cost Management User Guide - Managing your costs with AWS Budgets

q: An administrator of the management account of an AWS organization must turn on cost allocation tags and request backfills. Which console is used?
options: AWS Trusted Advisor checks console
AWS Billing and Cost Management
Amazon CloudWatch metrics console
AWS Config resource inventory console
explain: Cost allocation tag activation and backfill are managed from Billing and Cost Management, by the management account. The other consoles do not manage tags for cost reporting.
source: AWS docs: Billing User Guide - Backfill cost allocation tags

q: A stakeholder asks how the QuickSight name relates to the current AWS console naming. How is Amazon QuickSight related to Amazon Quick?
options: QuickSight replaced Amazon Quick and is now a standalone chatbot service for chat channels
Amazon Quick is the new name of the data pipeline service
QuickSight is now Amazon Quick Sight, a feature within Amazon Quick, and its APIs keep working
QuickSight and Amazon Quick are unrelated services that were launched in different AWS Regions
explain: QuickSight became Amazon Quick Sight, a feature within Amazon Quick, and existing QuickSight APIs and integrations continue to work.
source: AWS docs: Amazon Quick - What is Amazon Quick?

q: A company wants monthly cost reports per project for all training jobs and endpoints. Which tagging approach best supports this?
options: One catch-all tag named misc applied to every resource
Tags applied only to S3 buckets, not to training jobs or endpoints
Tag values changed at random every week so that each report shows a different breakdown
Project and CostCenter tags applied consistently to training jobs and endpoints at creation
explain: Consistent project and cost-center tags at creation let cost reports group spend by project. A single catch-all tag or tags on only one resource type cannot attribute cost.
source: AWS docs: Billing User Guide - Backfill cost allocation tags

q: A web team needs balanced compute, memory, and networking for its API servers. Which EC2 family is described as general purpose?
options: M general purpose, balancing compute, memory, and networking
R memory optimized for large in-memory data sets
G accelerated for graphics and floating-point work
P high-performance GPU instances for deep learning
explain: The M family is general purpose, balancing compute, memory, and networking. R is memory optimized, G is for graphics and accelerated work, and P is for high-performance GPU work.
source: AWS docs: Amazon EC2 instance types

q: Which THREE statements about SageMaker instance right-sizing are correct? (Select THREE.)
options: Inference Recommender Default jobs need only a model package ARN
Compute Optimizer analyzes utilization of resources already in use
Compute Optimizer creates new endpoints after each recommendation
Inference Recommender analyzes existing CloudTrail logs to size endpoints
Inference Recommender Advanced jobs run a custom load test with a traffic pattern
Both Inference Recommender job types return an initial instance count for autoscaling
explain: Default jobs need only the model package, Advanced jobs run custom load tests, and both return an initial instance count for autoscaling. Compute Optimizer analyzes running resources, while Inference Recommender does not analyze CloudTrail or create endpoints.
source: AWS docs: SageMaker AI Developer Guide - Recommendation jobs with Inference Recommender

q: A team runs agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and wants built-in dashboards for session count, latency, token usage, and errors. Which feature gives these detailed trace and metric dashboards?
options: AWS Trusted Advisor cost and security checks
AgentCore Observability
AWS Budgets monthly cost and usage alerts
Amazon Inspector vulnerability findings for images
explain: AgentCore Observability provides session, latency, token, and error metrics in CloudWatch dashboards. The other services do not monitor agent sessions.
source: AWS docs: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Developer Guide - Observability

q: Which TWO statements about Lambda provisioned concurrency are correct? (Select TWO.)
options: It is the right choice for asynchronous batch pipelines, which are the main beneficiaries
The configuration cannot be applied to the $LATEST version
Initialization cost is billed even when no requests arrive
Reserved concurrency and provisioned concurrency are the same setting
Provisioned concurrency costs nothing at all when the traffic on the function is low or idle
explain: Provisioned concurrency must target a published version or alias, and it is billed continuously, including initialization. It mainly helps latency-sensitive interactive workloads, and it is not the same as reserved concurrency.
source: AWS docs: Lambda Developer Guide - Configuring provisioned concurrency

q: A training team uses Managed Spot Training with MaxRuntimeInSeconds set to 7200. Which value of MaxWaitTimeInSeconds is valid?
options: 3600, because it must be smaller than MaxRuntimeInSeconds
7200, because it must equal MaxRuntimeInSeconds
10800, because it is greater than MaxRuntimeInSeconds
0, because the wait time is ignored for Spot
explain: MaxWaitTimeInSeconds must be larger than MaxRuntimeInSeconds, because it covers the runtime plus the time spent waiting for Spot capacity. Equal or smaller values are invalid.
source: AWS docs: SageMaker AI Developer Guide - Managed Spot Training
